title: Audit bridge: add audit-stream-router and sink provisioning for Private installs
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add audit-stream-router and sink provisioning to Private installer. Exposes configurable retention, sink mapping (S3/GCS/syslog/pubsub), Helm hooks for exporter lifecycle, and Terraform modules for sink IAM and buckets. No breaking changes; opt-in via installer flags.
description:
Context and motivation:
Redwood Private customers require deterministic audit export wiring during initial bootstrap and during upgrades. Previously the private installer surfaced audit-exporter as an optional post-install step that required manual sink provisioning and out-of-band configuration. That pattern caused missed exports during automated upgrades and made compliance automation brittle (ENG-5128, SEC-1023).

Summary of changes (high level):
- Introduce an audit-stream-router component that runs as a sidecar deployment in the Private control-plane. Router accepts local audit events and fans them to configured sinks with backpressure and retry semantics.
- Add Terraform modules (terraform/modules/audit_sinks/*) to provision sinks and IAM for S3, GCS, and GCP Pub/Sub targets. Modules are optional and idempotent.
- Add Helm chart pieces to redwood-private-installer chart: templates/audit-router-deployment.yaml, templates/audit-exporter-configmap.yaml, and hooks/pre-install-post-upgrade for sink registration and credential watering.
- Wire installer flags to enable/disable: --enable-audit-router, --audit-retention-days, --audit-sink-type(s). Default is disabled to preserve existing users.
- Add upgrade/rollback testing harness (installer/tests/audit_upgrade_test.sh) that simulates intermittent sink failures and validates no-loss guarantees for >72h retention window.

Commits (summary):
- Add router implementation and local buffer + checkpoint (commit: add audit-router core and metrics)
- Terraform modules for S3/GCS/pubsub with examples (commit: add terraform modules + docs)
- Helm chart templates and hooks with idempotent registration job (commit: helm: audit hooks + config)
- E2E tests and CI job (commit: add tests, az/gcp mock sinks)
- Fixes from review: permission tightening, short-circuit on disabled sinks, stronger healthprobe on hook jobs (commit: followups)

Files/touched (representative):
- installer/values.schema.yaml (new flags and validation)
- helm/redwood-private/templates/audit-router-deployment.yaml
- helm/redwood-private/templates/audit-exporter-configmap.yaml
- helm/redwood-private/templates/hooks/register-sink-job.yaml
- terraform/modules/audit_s3/main.tf, outputs.tf, iam.tf
- terraform/modules/audit_pubsub/*
- installer/tests/audit_upgrade_test.sh
- ci/pipelines/audit-e2e.yaml

Testing performed:
- Local VPC bootstrap (minikube + kind on CI) with mock syslog and a local S3-compatible endpoint (minio). Validated event ordering and at-least-once delivery under intermittent network drop.
- Terraform integration: apply/destroy runs against a test project, validated IAM roles scoped to bucket/publisher.
- Upgrade path test: install with router disabled, enable router via upgrade, validate backlog replay and sink registration works without dropping events.
- Rollback test: performed helm rollback of the router chart and validated exporter drains buffer to file before graceful shutdown.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Jonah Kim: "Nice approach with a local router to decouple installer timing from external sink readiness. Two requests: tighten IAM rules and add e2e that simulates long GC pauses."
- Maya: "Addressed IAM scoping in terraform/iam.tf and added e2e delay test. See commit 4f7b9a2 for test harness and notes."
- Evelyn Ortiz: "Helm hook can potentially run multiple times during retries; please make the job idempotent. Also ensure secrets are not printed in logs."
- Maya: "Made register-sink-job idempotent by checking CRD status; replaced kubectl echo with explicit non-verbose registration and redacted logs. Added unit test for hook idempotency."
- Samir Desai: "Circuit-breaker/backoff looks good. Can you expose metrics for in-flight buffer length?"
- Maya: "Added prometheus metrics: audit_router_buffer_length, audit_router_retry_count. Updated dashboard example in observability docs."

CI and checks: 
- lint: pass on first run
- unit tests: initial failure (audit router buffer edge-case), fixed in follow-up commit, re-ran -> pass
- integration (terraform): flaky on first run due to test credentials expiry, re-run with refreshed creds -> pass
- e2e: gated, passed in final run on 2026-02-17 (linux/amd64, kind cluster)
Overall CI status: pass.

Backward compatibility and migration notes:
- Installer flag --enable-audit-router defaults to false to avoid opt-in requirement for existing infra. Migration doc describes enabling during maintenance window; router will perform a one-time drain/replay for events persisted by previous exporter.
- Terraform modules are optional; if customers manage their own buckets/topics the installer will accept pre-existing sink configs.

Security & compliance review:
- SEC-1023: validated that IAM roles are least-privilege and that service accounts have short-lived credentials via workload identity where supported. Audit payloads optionally encrypted at rest by in-sink settings (SSE for S3, CMEK for GCS).

Release notes (user-facing):
- Private installer: opt-in audit-stream-router to reliably route audit logs to S3/GCS/PubSub or syslog. Helm hooks and Terraform modules provided to automate sink creation and wiring. Configurable retention and metrics exposed for monitoring.

Follow-ups (tracked):
- ENG-5201: add KMS/HSM integration for envelope encryption in-transit-to-sink.
- ENG-5234: add native FluentD/FluentBit adapter for customers who want to route through existing logging pipelines.

Merge details:
- Approved-by: Jonah Kim, Evelyn Ortiz, Samir Desai
- Method: squash merge into main on 2026-02-18 after final CI green

If you want to validate locally: see installer/README.md -> "Audit sink quickstart" and run installer/local_bootstrap.sh --enable-audit-router --audit-sink-type=minio to exercise end-to-end on a dev machine.

This PR is intentionally comprehensive to reduce manual steps during install/upgrade for regulated customers and to provide a clear automation path for audit sink provisioning during Private deployments.
